verses.original: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ
verses.transliteration: Epeidē eplērōsen panta ta rhēmata autou eis tas akoas tou laou eisēlthen eis Kapharnaoum
verses.literal: When Jesus had concluded . . . His discourse in the hearing of the people He went to Capernaum
verses.literalPt: Tendo Jesus concluído todos os seus discursos dirigidos ao povo, entrou em Cafarnaum.

verses.original: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος
verses.transliteration: Hekatontarchou de tinos doulos kakōs echōn ēmellen teleutan hos ēn autō entimos
verses.literal: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die
verses.literalPt: Um servo de um centurião, a quem este muito estimava, estava doente, quase à morte.

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: akousas de peri tou Iēsou apesteilen pros auton presbyterous tōn Ioudaiōn erōtōn auton hopōs elthōn diasōsē ton doulon autou
verses.literal: When the centurion heard about Jesus he sent some Jewish elders - to ask Him to come and heal his servant
verses.literalPt: O centurião, tendo ouvido falar a respeito de Jesus, enviou-lhe alguns anciãos dos judeus, pedindo-lhe que viesse curar o seu servo.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο
verses.transliteration: hoi de paragenomenoi pros ton Iēsoun parekaloun auton spoudaiōs legontes hoti Axios estin hō parexē touto
verses.literal: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly - This man is worthy to have You grant this
verses.literalPt: Estes, chegando-se a Jesus, com instância lhe suplicaram: Ele é digno de que lhe faças isso;

verses.original: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν
verses.transliteration: agapa gar to ethnos hēmōn kai tēn synagōgēn autos ōkodomēsen hēmin
verses.literal: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue
verses.literalPt: pois é amigo do nosso povo e ele mesmo edificou a nossa sinagoga.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ Κύριε μὴ σκύλλου οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous eporeueto syn autois ēdē de autou ou makran apechontos apo tēs oikias epempsen philous ho hekatontarchēs legōn autō Kyrie mē skyllou ou gar hikanos eimi hina hypo tēn stegēn mou eiselthēs
verses.literal: So Jesus went with them But when He was not far from the house the centurion sent friends with the message . . . Lord do not trouble Yourself for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof
verses.literalPt: Jesus foi com eles. Quando ia chegando à casa, o centurião enviou-lhe amigos para lhe dizer: Senhor, não te incomodes, porque não sou digno de que entres em minha casa.

verses.original: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου
verses.transliteration: dio oude emauton ēxiōsa pros se elthein alla eipe logō kai iathētō ho pais mou
verses.literal: That is why I did not consider myself worthy . . . to come to You But just say the word and my servant will be healed
verses.literalPt: Por isso, eu mesmo não me julguei digno de vir a ti; mas dize uma palavra, e o meu criado ficará são.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας καὶ λέγω τούτῳ Πορεύθητι καὶ πορεύεται καὶ ἄλλῳ Ἔρχου καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου Ποίησον τοῦτο καὶ ποιεῖ
verses.transliteration: kai gar egō anthrōpos eimi hypo exousian tassomenos echōn hyp’ emauton stratiōtas kai legō toutō Poreuthēti kai poreuetai kai allō Erchou kai erchetai kai tō doulō mou Poiēson touto kai poiei
verses.literal: For I myself am a man under authority with soldiers under me I tell one to go and he goes and another to come and he comes I tell . . . my servant to do something and he does it
verses.literalPt: Pois também eu sou homem sujeito à autoridade, e tenho soldados às minhas ordens, e digo a um: Vai ali, e ele vai; e a outro: Vem cá, e ele vem; e ao meu servo: Faze isto, e ele o faz.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν Λέγω ὑμῖν οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον
verses.transliteration: Akousas de tauta ho Iēsous ethaumasen auton kai strapheis tō akolouthounti autō ochlō eipen Legō hymin oude en tō Israēl tosautēn pistin heuron
verses.literal: When Jesus heard this He marveled at the centurion Turning to the crowd following Him He said I tell you not even in Israel have I found such great faith
verses.literalPt: Jesus, ouvindo isso, admirou-se e, virando-se para a multidão que o acompanhava, disse: Eu vos afirmo que nem mesmo em Israel achei tamanha fé.

verses.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα
verses.transliteration: kai hypostrepsantes eis ton oikon hoi pemphthentes heuron ton doulon hygiainonta
verses.literal: And when the messengers returned to the house they found the servant in good health
verses.literalPt: Voltando para casa os que haviam sido enviados, encontraram o servo de perfeita saúde.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto en tō hexēs eporeuthē eis polin kaloumenēn Nain kai syneporeuonto autō hoi mathētai autou kai ochlos polys
verses.literal: Soon afterward . . . . . . . . . Jesus went to a town called Nain His disciples went with Him accompanied by a large crowd
verses.literalPt: Em dia subsequente, dirigia-se Jesus para uma cidade chamada Naim, e iam com ele seus discípulos e uma grande multidão.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ
verses.transliteration: hōs de ēngisen tē pylē tēs poleōs kai idou exekomizeto tethnēkōs monogenēs huios tē mētri autou kai autē ēn chēra kai ochlos tēs poleōs hikanos ēn syn autē
verses.literal: As He approached the town gate He saw a dead man being carried out the only son of his mother and she was a widow And a large crowd from the town was with her
verses.literalPt: Ao aproximar-se ele da porta da cidade, eis que levavam para fora um defunto, filho único de sua mãe, que era viúva; e vinha com ela muita gente da cidade.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ Κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Μὴ κλαῖε
verses.transliteration: kai idōn autēn ho Kyrios esplanchnisthē ep’ autē kai eipen autē Mē klaie
verses.literal: When the Lord saw her He had compassion on her and said Do not weep
verses.literalPt: Logo que o Senhor a viu, compadeceu-se dela e disse-lhe: Não chores!

verses.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν καὶ εἶπεν Νεανίσκε σοὶ λέγω ἐγέρθητι
verses.transliteration: Kai proselthōn hēpsato tēs sorou hoi de bastazontes estēsan kai eipen Neaniske soi legō egerthēti
verses.literal: Then He went up and touched the coffin and those carrying it stood still Young man He said I tell you get up
verses.literalPt: Chegando-se, tocou o esquife e, parando os que o conduziam, disse: Moço, eu te mando: levanta-te!

verses.original: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai anekathisen ho nekros kai ērxato lalein kai edōken auton tē mētri autou
verses.literal: And the dead man sat up and began to speak Then Jesus gave him back to his mother
verses.literalPt: Aquele que havia estado morto sentou-se e começou a falar; e Jesus o entregou à mãe dele.

verses.original: Ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Elaben de phobos pantas kai edoxazon ton Theon legontes hoti Prophētēs megas ēgerthē en hēmin kai hoti Epeskepsato ho Theos ton laon autou
verses.literal: A sense of awe swept over all of them and they glorified God A great prophet has appeared among us - they said - God has visited His people
verses.literalPt: Todos ficaram cheios de medo e glorificaram a Deus, dizendo: Um grande profeta levantou-se entre nós; e: Deus visitou ao seu povo.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ
verses.transliteration: kai exēlthen ho logos houtos en holē tē Ioudaia peri autou kai pasē tē perichōrō
verses.literal: And the news about Jesus spread throughout . . . Judea and all the surrounding region
verses.literalPt: A notícia disso se divulgou por toda a Judeia e por toda a circunvizinhança.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων
verses.transliteration: Kai apēngeilan Iōannē hoi mathētai autou peri pantōn toutōn
verses.literal: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things
verses.literalPt: Todas essas coisas foram contadas a João pelos seus discípulos.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν
verses.transliteration: kai proskalesamenos dyo tinas tōn mathētōn autou ho Iōannēs epempsen pros ton Kyrion legōn Sy ei ho erchomenos ē allon prosdokōmen
verses.literal: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord Are You the One who was to come or should we look for someone else
verses.literalPt: João, chamando dois deles, enviou-os ao Senhor para perguntar: És tu aquele que há de vir ou havemos de esperar outro?

verses.original: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν
verses.transliteration: Paragenomenoi de pros auton hoi andres eipan Iōannēs ho Baptistēs apesteilen hēmas pros se legōn Sy ei ho erchomenos ē allon prosdokōmen
verses.literal: When the men came to Jesus they said John the Baptist sent us to ask Are You the One who was to come or should we look for someone else
verses.literalPt: Quando esses homens chegaram a Jesus, disseram: João Batista enviou-nos para te perguntar: És tu aquele que há de vir ou havemos de esperar outro?

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν
verses.transliteration: En ekeinē tē hōra etherapeusen pollous apo nosōn kai mastigōn kai pneumatōn ponērōn kai typhlois pollois echarisato blepein
verses.literal: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases afflictions and evil spirits and He gave sight to many who were blind
verses.literalPt: Na mesma hora, curou Jesus a muitos de moléstias, de flagelos e de espíritos malignos; e deu vista a muitos cegos.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται
verses.transliteration: kai apokritheis eipen autois Poreuthentes apangeilate Iōannē ha eidete kai ēkousate typhloi anablepousin chōloi peripatousin leproi katharizontai kai kōphoi akouousin nekroi egeirontai ptōchoi euangelizontai
verses.literal: So He replied . . . . . . Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard The blind receive sight the lame walk the lepers are cleansed the deaf hear the dead are raised and the good news is preached to the poor
verses.literalPt: Então, lhes respondeu: Ide contar a João o que vistes e ouvistes: os cegos veem, os coxos andam, os leprosos ficam limpos, os surdos ouvem, os mortos são ressuscitados, aos pobres anuncia-se-lhes o evangelho.

verses.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί
verses.transliteration: kai makarios estin hos ean mē skandalisthē en emoi
verses.literal: Blessed is the one who does not fall away . . . . . . on account of Me
verses.literalPt: E bem-aventurado é aquele que não achar em mim motivo de tropeço.

verses.original: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον
verses.transliteration: Apelthontōn de tōn angelōn Iōannou ērxato legein pros tous ochlous peri Iōannou Ti exēlthate eis tēn erēmon theasasthai kalamon hypo anemou saleuomenon
verses.literal: After John’s messengers had left Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John What did you go out into the wilderness to see A reed swaying in the wind
verses.literalPt: Partidos que foram os mensageiros de João, começou Jesus a falar ao povo a respeito de João: Que saístes a ver no deserto? Uma cana agitada pelo vento?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν
verses.transliteration: alla ti exēlthate idein anthrōpon en malakois himatiois ēmphiesmenon idou hoi en himatismō endoxō kai tryphē hyparchontes en tois basileiois eisin
verses.literal: Otherwise what did you go out to see A man dressed in fine clothes Look those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces
verses.literalPt: Mas que saístes a ver? um homem vestido de roupas finas? Os que se vestem ricamente e vivem no luxo, assistem nos palácios dos reis.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν προφήτην ναί λέγω ὑμῖν καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου
verses.transliteration: Alla ti exēlthate idein prophētēn nai legō hymin kai perissoteron prophētou
verses.literal: What then did you go out to see A prophet Yes I tell you and more than a prophet
verses.literalPt: Mas que saístes a ver? Um profeta? Sim, vos digo, e muito mais do que profeta.

verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου Ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου
verses.transliteration: houtos estin peri hou gegraptai Idou apostellō ton angelon mou pro prosōpou sou Hos kataskeuasei tēn hodon sou emprosthen sou
verses.literal: This is the one about whom it is written Behold I will send My messenger ahead of You . . . . . . who will prepare Your way before You
verses.literalPt: Este é aquele de quem está escrito: Eis aí envio eu ante a tua face o meu anjo, que há de preparar o teu caminho diante de ti.

verses.original: Λέγω ὑμῖν μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Legō hymin meizōn en gennētois gynaikōn Iōannou oudeis estin ho de mikroteros en tē basileia tou Theou meizōn autou estin
verses.literal: I tell you among those born of women there is no one greater than John yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he
verses.literalPt: Eu vos digo: entre os nascidos de mulher, não há nenhum maior do que João; mas o que é menor no reino de Deus é maior do que ele.

verses.original: Καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν Θεόν βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου
verses.transliteration: Kai pas ho laos akousas kai hoi telōnai edikaiōsan ton Theon baptisthentes to baptisma Iōannou
verses.literal: All the people who heard this even the tax collectors acknowledged God’s justice . . . . . . For they had received the baptism . . . . . . of John
verses.literalPt: Ao ouvir isso, todo o povo e até os publicanos reconheceram a justiça de Deus, sendo batizados com o batismo de João;

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: hoi de Pharisaioi kai hoi nomikoi tēn boulēn tou Theou ēthetēsan eis heautous mē baptisthentes hyp’ autou
verses.literal: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected - God’s purpose for themselves because they had not been baptized by John
verses.literalPt: mas os fariseus e os doutores da lei frustraram o desígnio de Deus quanto a si mesmos, não sendo batizados por ele.

verses.original: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι
verses.transliteration: Tini oun homoiōsō tous anthrōpous tēs geneas tautēs kai tini eisin homoioi
verses.literal: To what then can I compare the men of this generation What are they like
verses.literalPt: A que, pois, compararei os homens desta geração, e a que são eles semelhantes?

verses.original: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις ἃ λέγει Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε Ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε
verses.transliteration: homoioi eisin paidiois tois en agora kathēmenois kai prosphōnousin allēlois ha legei Ēulēsamen hymin kai ouk ōrchēsasthe Ethrēnēsamen kai ouk eklausate
verses.literal: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another . . . . . . We played the flute for you and you did not dance we sang a dirge and you did not weep
verses.literalPt: São semelhantes aos meninos que se assentam na praça e gritam uns para os outros: Nós vos tocamos flauta, e vós não dançastes; entoamos lamentações, e não pranteastes.

verses.original: Ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον καὶ λέγετε Δαιμόνιον ἔχει
verses.transliteration: Elēlythen gar Iōannēs ho Baptistēs mē esthiōn arton mēte pinōn oinon kai legete Daimonion echei
verses.literal: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine and you say He has a demon
verses.literalPt: Pois veio João Batista, não comendo pão, nem bebendo vinho, e dizeis: Ele tem demônio!

verses.original: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων καὶ λέγετε Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν
verses.transliteration: elēlythen ho Huios tou anthrōpou esthiōn kai pinōn kai legete Idou anthrōpos phagos kai oinopotēs philos telōnōn kai hamartōlōn
verses.literal: The Son of Man came eating and drinking and you say Look at this glutton and drunkard a friend of tax collectors and sinners
verses.literalPt: Veio o Filho do Homem, comendo e bebendo, e dizeis: Eis um homem glutão e bebedor de vinho, amigo de publicanos e pecadores?

verses.original: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: kai edikaiōthē hē sophia apo pantōn tōn teknōn autēs
verses.literal: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children
verses.literalPt: Contudo a sabedoria é justificada por todos os seus filhos.

verses.original: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη
verses.transliteration: Ērōta de tis auton tōn Pharisaiōn hina phagē met’ autou kai eiselthōn eis ton oikon tou Pharisaiou kateklithē
verses.literal: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him and He entered . . . the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table
verses.literalPt: Um dos fariseus convidou-o para jantar com ele. Jesus, entrando na casa do fariseu, tomou lugar à mesa.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου
verses.transliteration: kai idou gynē hētis ēn en tē polei hamartōlos kai epignousa hoti katakeitai en tē oikia tou Pharisaiou komisasa alabastron myrou
verses.literal: When . . . a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there she brought an alabaster jar of perfume
verses.literalPt: Havia na cidade uma mulher que era pecadora; ela, sabendo que ele estava jantando na casa do fariseu, trouxe um vaso de alabastro com perfume; e,

verses.original: καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ
verses.transliteration: kai stasa opisō para tous podas autou klaiousa tois dakrysin ērxato brechein tous podas autou kai tais thrixin tēs kephalēs autēs exemassen kai katephilei tous podas autou kai ēleiphen tō myrō
verses.literal: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair . . . . . . . . . Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume
verses.literalPt: pondo-se-lhe aos pés, chorando, começou a regá-los com lágrimas, e os enxugava com os cabelos da sua cabeça, e beijava-lhe os pés, e ungia-os com o perfume.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Idōn de ho Pharisaios ho kalesas auton eipen en heautō legōn Houtos ei ēn prophētēs eginōsken an tis kai potapē hē gynē hētis haptetai autou hoti hamartōlos estin
verses.literal: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this he said to himself If this man were a prophet He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him for she is a sinner
verses.literalPt: Ao ver isso, o fariseu que o convidara dizia consigo: Se este homem fosse profeta, saberia quem é a que o toca e que sorte de mulher é, pois é uma pecadora.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Σίμων ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν Ὁ δέ Διδάσκαλε εἰπέ φησίν
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen pros auton Simōn echō soi ti eipein Ho de Didaskale eipe phēsin
verses.literal: But Jesus answered . . . . . . him Simon I have something to tell you Tell me Teacher - he said
verses.literalPt: Disse Jesus ao fariseu: Simão, tenho uma coisa para te dizer. Ele respondeu: Dize-a, Mestre.

verses.original: Δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα
verses.transliteration: Dyo chreopheiletai ēsan danistē tini ho heis ōpheilen dēnaria pentakosia ho de heteros pentēkonta
verses.literal: Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender One owed him five hundred denarii and the other fifty
verses.literalPt: Certo credor tinha dois devedores: um lhe devia quinhentos denários, e o outro, cinquenta.

verses.original: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: mē echontōn autōn apodounai amphoterois echarisato tis oun autōn pleion agapēsei auton
verses.literal: When they were unable . . . to repay him he forgave both of them Which one then will love him more
verses.literalPt: Não tendo nenhum dos dois com que pagar, perdoou a dívida a ambos. Qual deles, portanto, o amará mais?

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis Simōn eipen Hypolambanō hoti hō to pleion echarisato Ho de eipen autō Orthōs ekrinas
verses.literal: I suppose the one who was forgiven more Simon replied . . . You have judged correctly - Jesus said
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Simão: Suponho que aquele a quem mais perdoou. Replicou-lhe: Julgaste bem.

verses.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν
verses.transliteration: Kai strapheis pros tēn gynaika tō Simōni ephē Blepeis tautēn tēn gynaika eisēlthon sou eis tēn oikian hydōr moi epi podas ouk edōkas hautē de tois dakrysin ebrexen mou tous podas kai tais thrixin autēs exemaxen
verses.literal: And turning toward the woman He said to Simon Do you see this woman When I entered . . . your house you did not give Me . . . water for My feet but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair
verses.literalPt: Virando-se para a mulher, disse a Simão: Vês esta mulher? Entrei em tua casa e não me deste água para os pés; mas esta mos regou com lágrimas e os enxugou com os seus cabelos.

verses.original: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας αὕτη δὲ ἀφ’ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας
verses.transliteration: philēma moi ouk edōkas hautē de aph’ hēs eisēlthon ou dielipen kataphilousa mou tous podas
verses.literal: You did not greet Me with a kiss but she has not stopped kissing My feet since . . . I arrived
verses.literalPt: Não me deste ósculo; ela, porém, desde que entrei, não cessou de beijar-me os pés.

verses.original: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου
verses.transliteration: elaiō tēn kephalēn mou ouk ēleipsas hautē de myrō ēleipsen tous podas mou
verses.literal: You did not anoint My head with oil but she has anointed My feet with perfume
verses.literalPt: Não ungiste a minha cabeça com óleo, mas esta com perfume ungiu os meus pés.

verses.original: οὗ χάριν λέγω σοι ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ
verses.transliteration: hou charin legō soi apheōntai hai hamartiai autēs hai pollai hoti ēgapēsen poly hō de oligon aphietai oligon agapa
verses.literal: Therefore I tell you her many sins have been forgiven for she has loved much But he who has been forgiven little loves little
verses.literalPt: Por isso, te digo: Perdoados lhe são os seus pecados, que são muitos, porque ela muito amou; mas aquele a quem pouco se perdoa pouco ama.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι
verses.transliteration: Eipen de autē Apheōntai sou hai hamartiai
verses.literal: Then Jesus said to her Your sins are forgiven
verses.literalPt: Disse à mulher: Perdoados são os teus pecados.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν
verses.transliteration: Kai ērxanto hoi synanakeimenoi legein en heautois Tis houtos estin hos kai hamartias aphiēsin
verses.literal: But those at the table began to say to themselves Who is this who even forgives sins
verses.literalPt: Os que estavam com ele à mesa começaram a dizer consigo mesmos: Quem é este que até perdoa pecados?

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην
verses.transliteration: Eipen de pros tēn gynaika Hē pistis sou sesōken se poreuou eis eirēnēn
verses.literal: And Jesus told . . . the woman Your faith has saved you go in peace
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus disse à mulher: A tua fé te salvou; vai-te em paz.
